KEY MESSAGE 1...A Noreaster will impact at least Downeast Maine
this weekend into Monday and possibly Tuesday, bringing gusty 
winds, high surf, and periods of rain.

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...
This morning the center of low pressure that is this Noreaster
is approx 110mi SE of New York City. It is slowly drifting NW
this morning towards the NJ/NY coastline. A large occlusion is
wrapped up just south of Cape Cod with a triple point near
Georges Bank. Satellite imagery is showing moisture advecting 
north in Maine from the the Atlantic which extends back to the
Bahamas. This has increased PWATs over Downeast Maine into the
175-200 percent of normal range for late September. At the same
time a strong 1028mb high pressure system sits over Central
Quebec with a 584dam 500mb ridge. The placement of the ridge and
North Atlantic low pressure near Greenland is preventing this
Noreaster from moving and nearly cutoff from the flow. 

Throughout the day expecting the Noreaster low pressure to 
drift closer to NYC as surface high drifts into the Maritimes. 
This will result in lessening precip chances across the CWA 
today. Tonight, the 500mb ridge will fold over and shift out 
over the North Atlantic which will allow the upper level low of 
this Noreaster to lift back into the mid latitude westerlies. 
This will begin to push the surface low northward into Southern 
New England as it slowly begins to weaken. The northerly 
movement will allow for increasing POPs across the entire CWA 
tonight into Monday and lasting into Tuesday with periods of 
rain expected. Overall, the wind field will weaken as the sfc 
low pressure lifts N then NE across the Gulf of Maine. Then by 
Tuesday afternoon the system will be exiting east across Nova 
Scotia. Here is what to expect for the various components of the
storm:

Periods of Rain...Rain chances will be far greater Downeast than
northern areas for this AM, tapering to showers during the day,
then areawide increasing POPs tonight lasting into Tuesday AM.
Although there remains significant uncertainty how many periods
of rain develop the overall trend has been consistent in lower
values across the area through Tuesday AM. However, with PWATs
areawide eventually up to around 190 percent of normal we can
expect some beneficial rainfall. The best beneficial rainfall
will be across the Bangor Region to far Southern Aroostook
County and points southward to the Downeast coast. It is here
that 0.6-1 inch is expected for totals, north of here
significant uncertainty exists due to dry air, totals in
northern areas generally 0.1-0.3 inch. We do not expect any
flooding concerns anywhere given the D1-D3 drought conditions.
In fact nearly all of the rainfall will likely be absorbed into
the near surface ground and very unlikely any water gets into
the rivers and streams. Rivers and streams are currently in the
1-15th percentile range with many approaching top 5 lowest flows
on record. 

Breezy Winds...Winds from the northeast will be the gustiest 
through Monday AM and begin to weaken into the afternoon and
Monday night. Winds will be stronger the further south you go 
but will top out around 25 mph across Bangor and the Downeast 
with the system remaining so far south of the CWA. Isolated 
higher gusts possible especially near the Downeast coastline
exposed to the NE winds across the open waters. We don't 
anticipate impacts from the wind other than maybe a very few
isolated power outages Downeast.

High Surf...Seas near the shore will be fairly rough with 4-8 
ft seas, much of it as a longer period south/southeast swell. We
are not expecting impactful coastal flooding, though waves 
breaking on the rocks will be hazardous for any onlookers. 
Conditions should be a bit more hazardous for coastal Hancock 
than coastal Washington. Conditions slowly ease tonight into 
Monday.
